newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: KAL crash victims family in Seoul stage sit-in.
newsitem.headline: KAL crash victims family in Seoul stage sit-in.

text.p: About 50 relatives of victims of the Korean Air Lines crash staged a sit-in on Thursday at a KAL building in Seoul demanding information about their loved ones.
Family members handed out leaflets in the street demanding better cooperation from KAL and government officials, witnesses said.
Police officers were posted along the street side to prevent the protesters from blocking traffic.
More than 100 people have been waiting at the centre for relatives set up at the building close to Kimpo airport after the KAL Boeing 747 crashed on the Pacific island of Guam early on Wednesday.
The families demanded that a clear list of those known to be dead be released.
Late on Thursday, officials in Guam said there were now just 27 survivors after three injured people died in hospital. Altogether, 74 people were confirmed dead and 153 remained missing.
"I wish they would just give us any information," said a woman holding a young child as tears welled in her eyes. "No one is telling us anything."
